newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold starts to feel Indian import demand.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold starts to feel Indian import demand.

text.p: Indian demand for gold from the Gulf re-export centre of Dubai shows signs of robust health entering the fourth quarter festival and wedding season, Dubai bullion traders said on Sunday.
Weaker gold prices, a stronger rupee, prospects for a good Indian harvest and an attractive Dubai-India arbitrage helped a gradual upturn in trade after a summer lull.
"Shipments to India are going very well. Demand is not depressed there," a regular supplier to India said.
Research group Gold Fields Mineral Services (GFMS) reported last week that a uniformly good monsoon season across India this year augured well for physical demand in the coming months.
The Gulf emirate of Dubai is the main feeder market into India, the world's single largest gold consuming state.
Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola bar (TT) -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted by traders at 5,267 UAE dirhmams ($1,435.15), down 18 dirhams on the week.
TT bar price in Bombay was assessed at $1,680, giving traders a possible 17 percent margin on paper.

International spot gold was last quoted on Saturday at $380.90-40 an ounce, knocked down to its lowest level since July on weakness in silver markets and an exodus of investment funds from the yellow metal.
Ten gram bars were quoted at 450 dirhams, down one dirham.
Silver was assesssed on Sunday at $157 an ounce in Dubai and $199 in Bombay.
The extent of the summer lull in Dubai business turnover was reflected in import and re-export figures released by the World Gold Council and customs officials in Dubai on Sunday.
Gold imports into the Gulf Arab emirate of Dubai fell 1.04 tonnes to 28.848 tonnes in August, the World Gold Council in Dubai reported.
Silver re-exports from Dubai to India slumped to 48.2 tonnes in August from 88.8 tonnes the previous month, according to Dubai customs figures.
Switzerland remained the main gold supplier to Dubai at 21.378 tonnes down from 22.331 in July, followed by Britain at 6.264 tonnes down from 6.451 tonnes.
Total bullion imports into Dubai totalled 228 tonnes in between January and August, up from 219 tonnes in the same period last year.
Dubai bullion trade to Pakistan was still subdued in contrast to India shipments, traders said.
"Pakistan is very slow nowadays. More illegal gold is being sold there," a Dubai-based supplier to Pakistan said. ($1=3.67 UAE dirhams)
